propositions: Mirror Guard workflow runs fail on a single instantaneous sample of transient, self-healing Gerrit–GitHub replication lag (~15s post-submit divergence), reds the run unnecessarily while a rerun 16 minutes later passes

The module's design (docstring lines 47–50) and secondary CloudWatch watcher (monitoring_ws7.tf 2x5-min sustained window) both expect lag absorption via an evaluation window, but the primary workflow watcher (mirror-guard.yml) implements no window and maps one diverged sample to exit 1
Incomplete-implementation defect: the designed lag-tolerance capability was never wired into the workflow surface despite being shipped in the introducing commit d96628c9dca; no later change broke it

Fix adds an in-process `replication_check_with_lag_tolerance` wrapper that re-samples up to 3 times (45s apart, ~90s total window) and returns healthy only when convergence is achieved or on first in-sync/missing-SHA samples, keeping unhealthy divergence that persists across the window
Any non-converged divergence still fails (no weakening); GitHub-ahead/foreign divergence never converges to Gerrit SHA so it remains loud every run
Portable implementation: tolerance lives in the module CLI path, works under any scheduler, and is tunable via --lag-attempts and --lag-delay flags
